$comment:
Marks nobody may take as a plugin id or wear as a display name without the rightsholder saying so. This is a bot-only policy file — tools/validate.mjs does not read it — which is why it lives under bot/ rather than in policy/, where the files both halves share live.

What it is for: `spotify-controller` and `Spotify Controller` are not descriptions, they are claims to be Spotify's. The store card shows a name and an author string and nothing else, so a name that reads as first-party from the vendor IS the impersonation. What it is NOT for: stopping anyone from saying which service their plugin talks to. `Music controls for Spotify` is a description of a third-party plugin and passes, because the mark is not the leading token and the name does not read as the vendor's own.

The rule, precisely: a listing is refused when the FOLDED id equals a mark or its FIRST hyphen-separated component is one, or when the folded display name's FIRST word is one. A mark anywhere else passes, because `music-for-spotify` and `notes-sync-notion` are descriptions of third-party plugins and refusing them would be refusing honesty. Anything else is allowed. Two knobs so an honest name is not caught: `allow_repo_owners` lets a mark's real owner list under it (matched against the repository's owner login, which the ownership check has already proved), and `allow_ids` is the explicit, reviewed exception list.

This catches lazy impersonation and honest mistakes. It does not catch homoglyphs of a mark that are not in tools/lib/ids.mjs's fold table, transliterations, or a determined person with a thesaurus — and docs/BOT-CHECKS.md says so rather than implying a denylist is a defence.

allow_ids.$comment: id -> the issue or pull request where a human agreed. An entry with no reference is an entry nobody reviewed.
allow_ids.telegram-client: seed listing, first-party example, predates this policy — renamed at the next major version
allow_ids.web-chat: no mark; listed here only because `chat` reads like one to a skim
